description: The Nova Raiders are a creative and determined team competing in the Space Mission Design Game. Combining innovation, teamwork, and strategic thinking, we aim to design an exciting and effective space mission that tackles challenges beyond Earth. With our sights set on victory, The Nova Raiders are ready to push boundaries, explore new possibilities, and win the hackathon.
summary: Space Mission Cube is a free browser game where you inspect real NASA spacecraft, find what could go wrong, redesign them, then launch and fly your design. Players pick one of five missions: Curiosity, Perseverance, the James Webb Space Telescope, Hubble, or Apollo 11’s Lunar Module. Each one assembles itself in 3D. You scan every part and connection for hidden dangers, which are randomized each time. Then you fix them in the Trade-Off Workshop, a Rubik’s-cube-style puzzle: fixing one problem, like mass, can break another, like power, science, or budget. Solve it, and you watch a cinematic launch and the real journey to the destination, then play the mission. It answers the challenge by turning real mission design trade-offs into something anyone can play. Three levels (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced) change the vocabulary and difficulty, so it works for beginners and engineers alike. It runs on computers, tablets, and phones with nothing to install.
details:
We built Space Mission Cube to show why spacecraft design is about trade-offs. Real missions run into this constantly: a heavier instrument needs a bigger rocket, more power, and more budget.

What it does: Players choose a level, then a spacecraft. They inspect every part, run a diagnostic that finds randomized dangers, and fix them in the Trade-Off Workshop by swapping parts until mass, power, science, and budget all pass. Then they launch their design, see the real journey (a parking orbit, then a burn to Mars, or a direct trip to L2 for Webb), and play the mission.

Benefits and impact: Students learn how engineers weigh competing requirements, without needing any background. A word helper and three levels make it usable from beginners to advanced learners.

Tools: HTML, JavaScript, and Tailwind CSS, with Three.js for the 3D graphics and Web Audio for the sound effects. The game was built with help from Claude Code.

Creativity: The logo is a Rubik’s Cube because on a spacecraft, fixing one thing can break another, and the whole game is built around that idea.
